what_its_for: Paliperidone is used to treat schizophrenia (a mental health condition that affects how you think, feel, and behave) and schizoaffective disorder (a condition that combines symptoms of schizophrenia with mood disorder symptoms like depression or mania). It helps reduce hallucinations (hearing or seeing things that are not there), delusions (false beliefs), and disorganized thinking.
how_to_take: Paliperidone comes as a tablet you swallow whole once a day, or as a long-acting injectable shot given by your doctor or nurse. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or split it. You may take the tablet with or without food, but try to take it the same way each time. Do not be alarmed if you see something in your stool that looks like the tablet — this is just the empty shell and is normal. For the injectable form, your healthcare provider will give you the shot, usually in your upper arm or buttock muscle.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you. For tablets, the usual starting dose for adults is 6 mg once daily, and it can be adjusted between 3 mg and 12 mg per day. For the monthly injection (Invega Sustenna), you will receive two starting shots and then one shot every month. For the 3-month injection (Invega Trinza) or 6-month injection (Invega Hafyera), your doctor will switch you to these after you have been stable on the monthly injection. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: For tablets: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember the same day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. For injections: Contact your doctor or clinic right away if you miss a scheduled injection appointment. It is very important to keep all injection appointments to keep your symptoms under control.
storage: Store paliperidone tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep them away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store in a dry place — do not store in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Injectable forms are stored and handled by your healthcare provider, so you do not need to worry about storing those at home.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking paliperidone, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Do not drive a car, operate heavy machinery, or do other activities that require you to be alert until you know how this medication affects you. Avoid getting overheated or becoming dehydrated — drink plenty of fluids, especially in hot weather or during exercise. Avoid taking other medications (including over-the-counter drugs and supplements) without checking with your doctor first, especially other antipsychotics or medicines that cause drowsiness. Avoid suddenly stopping this medication without talking to your doctor.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: stiff muscles, high fever, confusion, or irregular heartbeat (signs of a rare but serious condition called Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome); uncontrollable movements of your face, tongue, or body (signs of a condition called tardive dyskinesia); feeling faint, lightheaded, or dizzy when standing up; difficulty swallowing; seizures; prolonged or painful erection (in males); signs of high blood sugar such as increased thirst, frequent urination, or blurry vision; thoughts of harming yourself or others; or any severe allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: Some improvement in symptoms such as agitation or sleep problems may be noticed within the first few days of starting treatment. However, the full benefit of paliperidone — including reduced hallucinations and clearer thinking — may take several weeks (usually 4 to 6 weeks or longer). It is important to keep taking the medication even if you do not feel better right away. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and over): Use with caution. Older adults with dementia-related psychosis should not use this medication, as it may increase the risk of stroke or death. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose. Kidney problems: Your doctor may need to lower your dose if you have kidney disease. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Taking antipsychotics in the third trimester may cause temporary muscle stiffness or withdrawal symptoms in the newborn. Breastfeeding: Paliperidone may pass into breast milk. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor before breastfeeding. Children and teenagers: Paliperidone tablets are approved for children aged 12 and older for schizophrenia. The injectable forms are generally for adults only. Your doctor will determine the safest dose based on your child's weight.
